clue.text: Do OK but appear to withdraw?

parts.note: to come up is to appear or arise, as a topic comes up
to scratch a horse or competitor is to withdraw it from a race

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about someone who performs adequately yet seems to be pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is the phrase read word by word: arrive, to, pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the required standard is doing well enough, an idiom from boxers toeing the line drawn on the floor.

clue.text: About to secure strongbox, where one may 8, giving nothing away

definitions.text: where one may 8, giving nothing away

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase for locking the box goes round the little word to

parts.note: to close a lid is to secure it
a strongbox is a chest for valuables, here the chest

explanation.surface: Someone about to lock up a strongbox while keeping their cards hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 in the clue stands for the answer to 8 down, a card player's phrase, so the definition pictures a player shielding a hand; 'strongbox' must be read as 'the chest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player holding the hand tight against their torso hides it from opponents, so the idiom means secretive.

clue.text: One that's near title losing time

indicators.note: losing means the abbreviation for time is dropped from the form of address

parts.note: Mister is a title put before a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone close to gaining a title runs out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is not about distance: it is an old word for stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Near in its older sense means tight-fisted, and a hoarder of money is exactly such a stingy person.

clue.text: Maintaining quiet air as river rises, take advantage of lift

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the word for exploit holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to use someone is to take advantage of them
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: in a down clue rising sends the river letter up to the top of the word for air

parts.note: an air is a tune, taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Some instruction about a lift where a quiet air plays while a river rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as river rises' needs no extra river: the tune word already contains the river letter, and in a down clue 'rises' lifts that letter to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to raise it up, an old verb synonym for lift.

clue.text: Race to join conversation that will make you smart

parts.note: to tear along is to race
gas is idle chatter or talk

explanation.surface: Advice to hurry and join a conversation that will make you clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' means sting, not clever: the definition is about stinging eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot-control chemicals sting the eyes, and smart is a verb meaning to feel a stinging pain.

clue.text: Ridiculing racist I thumped

indicators.note: thumped means battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racist is mocked and then punched.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire mocks its targets, so writing in that mode is ridiculing them.

clue.text: Get back from sports ground having finished

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
over means finished or ended

explanation.surface: Coming home from the playing field once the game has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something lost is to recover it, a plain synonym for get back.

clue.text: Condensation in carriages eventually shorted regular current

indicators.note: in places the moisture word inside the word for a line of carriages

parts.note: a train is a line of carriages
dew is moisture condensed from the air

indicators.note: eventually points at the final letter of shorted

explanation.surface: Condensation inside railway carriages finally causes an electrical short in the regular current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks electrical; it is an air current, and 'shorted' gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These are steady prevailing winds over the tropics, a reliable flow of air that sailing ships used.

clue.text: Be in full control of big bag on deck

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the bag word comes first

parts.note: a holdall is a large travelling bag
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A big bag sitting on the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship but is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing every advantage in a contest, like a player with every strong card, means being in charge.

clue.text: Our sister has no hesitation taking on worker with sharp eyes

indicators.note: taking on means adding the worker after what remains
has no means the hesitation sound is removed from the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Observer is the Sunday sister paper of the Guardian, where this clue appeared
er is the sound of hesitation
an ant is the standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A sister who no longer hesitates hires a worker with keen sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our sister' is the Guardian speaking of its Sunday sibling, The Observer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to notice things is watchful, which is what sharp-eyed means.

clue.text: Crop left to make slow progress

parts.note: a craw is the crop of a bird, the pouch in its gullet

explanation.surface: A harvest left in the field makes slow headway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' is not a harvest but a bird's throat pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward on hands and knees, or like traffic, is to advance very slowly.

clue.text: Not hard for fish to swallow a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: to swallow means take inside, so the word a goes into what remains
not means the hard letter is left out of the fish's name

parts.note: a herring is a common fish
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A fish that is reluctant to swallow a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: HERRING minus H gives ERRING, which swallows A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament hung from the lobe is a familiar kind of jewellery.

clue.text: I visited Mexican painter here in the south of France

definitions.text: here in the south of France

indicators.note: visited means the letter I calls in on, so sits inside, the painter's name

parts.note: Diego Rivera was a famous Mexican muralist

explanation.surface: Someone recalls calling on a Mexican painter who lived in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean coastal strip of south-east France, the Côte d'Azur, is the place the clue calls here.

clue.text: He fought a big cat: that's not on

indicators.note: not means the little word on is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A man took on a big cat in a fight, which is not on.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali was the boxing heavyweight champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The great heavyweight boxer is the man who fought, a definition by example.

clue.text: Terrifying woman's repeated power to knock out a grand bully

indicators.note: to knock out means the new letters push the thousand letter out and take its place

parts.note: an ogress is a terrifying female monster
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: repeated means the power letter appears twice

explanation.surface: A frightening woman uses force again and again to flatten a grand bully.
explanation.walkthrough: PP replaces G in OGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tyrannise or keep down by force is to bully, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Writer about to set up cheap material on eastern ruler

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the earlier letters above the rest
about means surrounding, so the writing tool goes round the other letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word to is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless stuff

explanation.surface: A writer about to make something from cheap material with an eastern ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' is not a measuring stick but a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or despot with great power is a ruler.

clue.text: Take action as point in dispute is dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the word is is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an issue is a point in dispute

explanation.surface: Someone goes to law as a contested point is abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to court against someone is taking legal action.

clue.text: Friendly girl in pink

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the colour

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A friendly girl dressed in pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and genial manners are cordial ones, a synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Blade decapitated pig

indicators.note: decapitated means the first letter, the head, is cut off

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A blade beheaded a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' looks like the weapon; it is the flat end of the rowing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat paddle end of a rowing pole is called its blade, and rowers call the whole thing a blade.

clue.text: Lid on trunk initially stuck out — cutter supplied

indicators.note: on means the head covering comes before the trunk word

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: out means the letter picked from stuck is removed

parts.note: the chest is the trunk of the body

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of stuck

explanation.surface: A lid on a tree trunk sticks out, supplied with a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' is the body's torso, not a tree; CHEST loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe is a tool for chopping, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: Greaser endlessly tough in awful weather

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the weather word

parts.note: hail is unpleasant falling ice

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: iron as an adjective means hard or tough, as in an iron will

explanation.surface: A greaser who is endlessly hard in terrible weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greaser' suggests a rocker, but is literal: something that greases.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade combed through the hair makes it slick, so it is a greaser.

clue.text: One touching line of smack sent for execution

parts.note: a smack is a taste or tang, as in a smack of garlic

indicators.note: execution means beheading, so the first letter of sent is cut off

explanation.surface: A line of smack is sent off to be used for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' is a hint of flavour, not a blow or drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this straight line meets a curve at a single point without crossing it.

clue.text: In inspiration, daughter shows liberality of mind

indicators.note: in places the daughter letter inside the word for inspiration

parts.note: inspiration is literally drawing in breath

explanation.surface: In a moment of inspiration, a daughter shows open-mindedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' means breathing in, not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth of mind is tolerance and wide outlook, the phrase the definition glosses.

clue.text: Rough and rude treatment for rabies at hospital

indicators.note: treatment here means working the letters over into a new shape

explanation.surface: Harsh and crude care given for rabies in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly and gruff like a bear describes someone rough-mannered and impolite.

clue.text: Unpredictable Cartman keeps an odd pet!

indicators.note: keeps means holding inside, so the cartoon name holds the pet

parts.note: Eric Cartman is a character in the cartoon South Park
a rat is an unusual pet

explanation.surface: A cartoon boy surprisingly keeps a strange pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is irregular or wayward cannot be predicted.

clue.text: Hail penetrating cavern

indicators.note: penetrating means the letters sit inside the word cavern

explanation.surface: Hailstones driving into a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather but is a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin greeting used in prayers and salutes is a way to hail someone.

clue.text: Carefully study gesture to transmit

parts.note: to con is to study carefully, an old word
a sign is a gesture

explanation.surface: Instructions to watch a hand signal closely before sending a message.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over or send goods is to dispatch or transmit them.

clue.text: Like some exercise? I carried back some French wine bottles

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so the wine letters enclose the rest

parts.note: AC, appellation contrôlée, marks some French wines

indicators.note: back means the phrase I bore is read in reverse

parts.note: bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: I carried back some French wine bottles, which counts as exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise that builds stamina by increasing oxygen use, like jogging, is described this way.

clue.text: Promoting English with plausible nonsense

indicators.note: in a down clue promoting sends letters upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: glib means smooth and plausible

explanation.surface: Promoting English with smooth talk is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge water is foul, so the word is slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: School almost suppressing artist's inspiration

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the school name holds the artist
almost means the last letter of the school name is dropped

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A school nearly crushes an artist's inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is an elite English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the nine Muses, the one for love poetry, a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Reader in church always involving ancient Shakespearean

indicators.note: involving means enfolding, so the poetic word for always goes round the character

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
Ancient Pistol is a braggart soldier in Shakespeare's history plays, ancient meaning ensign

explanation.surface: A church reader who is forever engaged with an old Shakespeare actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ancient' is a rank, ensign, and Pistol holds it in Henry IV and V.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the person who reads the Epistle aloud during a church service.

clue.text: Complications ensue as more points are added to graph

definitions.meaning: the stock phrase said when a story becomes more tangled

definitions.text: more points are added to graph
definitions.meaning: read literally, a chart drawing gets denser with more plotted marks

explanation.surface: As things get complicated, more data points go onto a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the plot literally as a graph that becomes denser.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom announces that a story is becoming more intricate, and a graph with extra points is literally denser.
